summary: Theodore Gabriel worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Stcherbatsky (1866–1942) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. An attested member of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1931, he taught numerous scholars.
Theophil Gubler worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.

Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Columbia and Princeton (1961–1963) and taught at both in 1961. He founded the An Quang Pagoda and the School of Youth for Social Service.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Delhi, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

Thierry Mathou (born 1963) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School and the Paris Institute of Political Studies, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Thierry Meynard (born 1963) is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Peking University under Yulie Lou. He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University around 2006 and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies in 2012.

Thinh Canh Quang specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and in 1994 was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Stanford University under William R. Hutchison and others. He was Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill from around 1993 to 2008.

Thomas Borchert specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He conducted PhD research at the University of Chicago under numerous faculty and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Queen Elizabeth School and Christ's College, Cambridge, he served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford from circa 1944 to 1976.
Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He was educated at Harvard University, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks.
Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) is a historian and archaeologist. Educated at Pomona College, he held posts at the University of Michigan from around 1986 to 1990 and at New York University around 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was an Indologist and historian educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, he later served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion.

Thomas H. Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne under Tom J. F. Tillemans, having also been supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer for his MA.

Thomas James Mazanec is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Calvin University, the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed doctoral work under Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and Wang Ping.

Thomas Jülch (born 1975) works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2006–2011) and served as a research fellow at Ghent University (attested 2019).
